title: 2018 AMC 8 Problem 22
statement: Point \(E\) is the midpoint of side \(\overline{CD}\) in square \(ABCD,\) and \(\overline{BE}\) meets diagonal \(\overline{AC}\) at \(F.\) The area of quadrilateral \(AFED\) is \(45.\) What is the area of \(ABCD?\)

solutions.text:
Let the square have side length \(s,\) and let \(H\) be the foot of the perpendicular from \(F\) to \(\overline{BC}.\) The right triangles \(CAB\) and \(CFH\) are similar, so \(CH=FH.\) Also, triangles \(BFH\) and \(BEC\) are similar, giving \[ \frac{FH}{EC}=\frac{BH}{BC}. \] Since \(EC=\frac{s}{2},\) \(BC=s,\) and \(BH=s-CH=s-FH,\) this becomes \(\frac{2FH}{s}=1-\frac{FH}{s},\) so \(FH=CH=\frac{s}{3}.\)

Thus triangle \(EFC\) has base \(EC=\frac{s}{2}\) and height \(CH=\frac{s}{3},\) so its area is \(\frac{s^2}{12}.\) Therefore \[\begin{aligned} [AFED]&=[\triangle ACD]-[\triangle EFC]\\ &=\dfrac{s^2}{2}-\dfrac{s^2}{12}\\ &=\dfrac{5s^2}{12}. \end{aligned}\] Since this area is \(45\), we get \(s^2=108\), the area of the square.
hints: Let the square have side length \(s\).
Find the small triangle cut from \(\triangle ACD\), then subtract it from half the square.
